title: OpenCode says attackers reached API keys and ran up charges on 1.4% of Console users
friendlyTitle: OpenCode says attackers used stored API keys and ran up some users' bills
summary: TechCrunch reports that OpenCode said attackers broke into an older part of OpenCode Console, the online place where some users store API keys for AI services. The company said 1.4% of Console users were affected, and that people who did not get an email were not. Co-founder Dax Raad said the open-source app and command-line tool were not affected, because those keys are not sent to OpenCode. Users reported unexpected charges in the hundreds of dollars, and a few above $1,000. Anthropic and Google blocked keys they believed were exposed. OpenAI said it worked with OpenCode to restore access and refund its API customers. OpenCode said refunds for unauthorised charges are underway.

whyItMatters: If you keep provider keys in a coding agent's hosted console, check for OpenCode's email and watch the bill, even if you did not run a job. The local tool is a different system. A key stored in a shared online workspace can spend money after you have closed the laptop.
